children: Saloni Shukla Mumbai: Non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) are reassessing short-tenure and EMI-based gold loans after a spike in early delinquencies in the September quarter, as borrowers accustomed to traditional bullet-repayment plans struggle to adjust to more frequent repayment schedules. Bajaj Finance has discontinued its short-tenure schemes, while Manappuram Finance is gradually shifting customers towards one-year loans.

Muthoot Finance and Shriram Finance have also reported an increase in overdue loans linked to changes in repayment structures, though the lenders maintain that the underlying portfolios remain adequately collateralised. The developments follow the Reserve Bank of India's revised gold-lending framework that took effect from April 1, 2026. Several lenders subsequently introduced new repayment products requiring periodic interest payments or equated monthly instalments (EMIs), unlike traditional bullet loans where principal and interest are payable at maturity.

Bajaj Finance posted a 1,047 crore rise in stage 2 gold loans during the September quarter, largely attributed to short-tenure schemes introduced following the regulatory changes. "We have, since August, stopped doing short-tenor schemes as a firm," vice chairman and managing director Rajeev Jain said at the company's earnings call. Management said around 550 crore of the affected portfolio had already returned to stage 1 by the time of the call.

title: Dodging Bullet Loans Hurt Gold NBFCs
